acceptanceCriteria: A builder working in a plain clone of origin/main can read a ticket created after the last committed .taskman snapshot (for example by pointing at the primary store read-only), or the refusal names the stale snapshot and how to reach the authoritative store instead of saying the ticket does not exist
A test covers the clone-read case: a ticket present in the journal but absent from the clone's snapshot returns the new answer, not a not-found error
docs/DOGFOOD.md or the corvint-tasks skill states how a lane clone reads its own ticket
body: Observed 2026-10-14 in the V1-1373 builder lane (plain clone of origin/main at d63c1c3a1, corvint-tasks from PATH): `corvint-tasks ticket show V1-1373` answered that the ticket "does not exist in this queue". V1-1373 was created earlier the same day and exists in the primary checkout's journal (.git/taskman). Expected: either the clone reads the ticket, or the refusal says the clone's queue snapshot is older than the ticket and names the authoritative store. Actual: a plain not-found error, which reads as if the ticket ID were wrong. Lanes currently work from orchestrator-written charters to get around it. Suspected cause: a clone has only the committed .taskman snapshot and no journal; not confirmed from the source.
title: corvint-tasks in a plain lane clone reports a ticket newer than the committed snapshot as nonexistent
